questions.q: What are the two sides of the basic accounting entry for an approved, accounted expense item?
options: A debit to an expense account and a credit to a liability account
A debit to cash and a credit to revenue
Two debits with no credit
A single entry with no debit or credit distinction
questions.explain: The expense account is debited and a liability account (owed to the employee or the card issuer) is credited, following standard double-entry accounting.

questions.q: What determines which liability account is credited for a given expense item?
options: The employee's job title
The time of day the item was entered
Whether the item was a cash expense or individual-liability card charge (Employee Expense Payable) versus a company-liability card charge (Corporate Card Payable)
The color of the receipt
questions.explain: The liability account credited depends on who the company owes: the employee for cash/individual-liability items, or the card issuer for company-liability items.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion Expenses generate accounting events for Subledger Accounting to interpret, rather than posting directly to the General Ledger?
options: Because direct posting is technically impossible in any Oracle module
Because Subledger Accounting is unrelated to Expenses
Because the General Ledger cannot accept expense transactions
To get the same audit trail, preview-before-posting capability, and consistent multi-currency/intercompany handling used by Payables and Receivables
questions.explain: Using Subledger Accounting gives Expenses the same architecture benefits already seen in Payables and Receivables, rather than needing separate custom logic.

questions.q: In Priya's itemized hotel folio example, why did the $21.00 personal movie charge NOT generate a liability credit?
options: Because it was flagged non-reimbursable, so the company isn't paying it even though it stays visible for policy tracking
Because itemization deletes non-reimbursable items entirely
Because movie charges are always tax-exempt
Because the amount was too small to matter
questions.explain: A non-reimbursable item is tracked for visibility but creates no company liability, since the company is not actually paying for it.

questions.q: Does the expense account debited for a Hotel charge change depending on whether it was paid in cash or on a corporate card?
options: Yes, cash and card charges always use completely different expense accounts
No, the expense account is the same either way; only the liability account credited differs
Expense accounts are never used for hotel charges
Only company-liability cards generate an expense account debit
questions.explain: The debit side (the expense account, like Travel & Lodging) stays the same regardless of payment method; only the credited liability account changes.
